reason: The current MaskedSASRec achieves authoritative macro validation HR@10=0.5800, supporting an isolated scoring-head experiment while retaining its backbone and objective. Candidate-independent query compression may limit discrimination across historical interests, but the results do not establish this cause. Historical cosine scoring and dropout-consistency failures favor preserving unnormalized tied scoring and existing supervision; successful jointly trained memory paths support testing candidate-conditioned context within one network. Model design and training/evaluation are the appropriate modules for implementing the head, maintaining loss equivalence, and exporting faithful predictions.

plan.model_design: Replace the fixed scoring head inside the current reference MaskedSASRec with candidate-conditioned attention pooling, retaining item_emb, item_bias, encoder, output, existing variable names, constructor arguments, forward(sequence), and predict(sequence, candidates). For each supervised position t and candidate c, form a learned attention query from concatenated features[t] and item_emb(c), attend through shared learned key/value projections over that example's encoded corrupted sequence using scaled dot products, and exclude sequence.eq(0) before softmax across positions. Concatenate the pooled context with features[t], apply one shared learned projection and LayerNorm, and score its unnormalized dot product with the tied candidate embedding plus jointly trained item_bias; do not introduce cosine normalization, independent scoring branches, or separately fitted components. Implement a shared score_candidates helper accepting encoded features, corrupted sequence, supervised row/position indices, and candidate IDs, supporting both per-query positives and shared negatives with deterministic query/candidate chunking. Keys and values must depend only on corrupted inputs, including mask representations, never reconstruction labels; preserve the bidirectional backbone and corruption scheme rather than importing historical relative-bias, convolution, consistency, or false-negative-filtering changes.
plan.training_evaluation: Update train_one to encode each corrupted sequence once and use score_candidates for positive and 256 shared uniform-negative logits, retaining target-collision masking, equal final-versus-auxiliary loss weighting, AdamW settings, gradient clipping, and all existing sampling hyperparameters. Bound forward and backward memory by chunking supervised positions and candidates, optionally checkpointing pooling computations, while assembling the identical sampled-softmax support and using global final/auxiliary counts so chunk boundaries do not change loss weighting. Preserve train_one, make_validation, evaluate, prediction_sequence, write_predict_script, and the exported predict signature; update checkpoint metadata and the predictor writer to reconstruct the modified architecture and strictly load exactly one newly trained selected checkpoint for each of the four category routes. Check finite gradients, padding exclusion, hidden-label independence of encoded memory, candidate-order equivariance, chunked-versus-unchunked scores and gradients, empty-history behavior, and exported-predictor parity without perturbing training RNG state. Retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], supplied splits and preprocessing seed 0, training/worker seed 42, isolated seed-42 validation with 200 users and 99 unique negatives, HR@10 selection with NDCG tie-breaking, PATIENCE=25, CATEGORY_SECONDS=2400, the environment-controlled 200-epoch default, trial-local artifacts, and single-GPU execution; report selected-checkpoint category and macro validation scores against 0.5800 with actual GPU cost under the shared budget, leaving authoritative evaluation and hidden-test inference to the host.
